title: Contextual sampling playbook for user-impacting route verdicts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Routing decisions (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants) currently emit coarse telemetry that makes it hard to tie user-visible regressions to specific policy changes or fallback events. We need a lightweight, privacy-conscious sampling playbook that captures high-signal examples when routing decisions potentially affect users (latency, quality, or cost regressions) without saturating logs or increasing storage costs.

Goal: Define an adaptive sampling strategy, a minimal verdict ledger schema, retention and storage tiers, and Console dashboards/alerts so engineers and SREs can rapidly debug wrong-region or fallback-model incidents and correlate them with SLO degradation. The playbook should be operationally safe (rate-limited), customer-aware (tiered sampling), and extensible for future policy signals.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A documented sampling algorithm (adaptive + stratified) implemented in the routing sidecar with feature flag toggle.

A2: Verdict ledger entries emitted for sampled requests containing the minimal schema (request_id, selected_region, selected_tier, model_variant, decision_reason, latency_ms, quality_signal, cost_delta_estimate, kv_cache_hit, routing_policy_version, timestamp).
A3: Sampled entries stored in hot store (7d) and archived to cold store (90d) with retention policy enforced and size budget set (max 12 GB/day global).
A4: Console dashboard showing sampled verdicts, per-region fallback rate, per-variant latency and quality histograms, and an alert when fallback rate increases >3x baseline for 10m.
A5: End-to-end tests that simulate: region outage -> increased fallback; model variant rollout -> quality regression; cost spike -> route change and sampled trace capture.
design_decisions: D1: Emit only sampled verdicts; full raw request bodies are never logged by default (PII rule).

D2: Sampling is adaptive: base rate by customer tier (P0 customers 1.0%, P1 0.5%, free 0.1%) plus multiplicative increases for impact signals (latency > p95, quality drop > 2% on eval prompts, cost delta > 30%).
D3: Use per-request impact_score to drive short bursts of 100% capture for affected users for 5 minutes (circuit-breaker style) to aid RCA, then exponentially decay to baseline sampling rate.
D4: Verdict ledger format is JSON lines (compact) and routed to the routing-observability kafka topic with a dedicated partitioning key (region:policy_version).
D5: Hot store will be ClickHouse for fast ad-hoc queries integrated into Console; cold store will be GCS/S3 with compact indexes for replay.
telemetry_schema_snippets: decision_reason: short enum (latency_pref, cost_pref, capacity_fallback, policy_pin, geo_restriction)
quality_signal: float (optional, from downstream evaluator or proxy score 0..1)
cost_delta_estimate: float (estimated token-cost delta vs baseline)
routing_policy_version: string (git sha or semantic), timestamp: iso8601
storage_and_retention: Hot store (ClickHouse): 7 days of full verdict rows, support fast Console filters and drilldowns.
Cold store (GCS/S3): 90 days archived gzipped JSONL; index files store request_id->offset for targeted replay.
Budget guard: global quota cap at 12 GB/day for verdicts; sampling algorithm must respect a configured cluster token bucket.
Access control: only SRE/Platform+owner teams can retrieve raw archived entries; Console shows redacted fields for general viewers.
sampling_strategy: Baseline stratified: sample by customer tier and region to ensure representative coverage.
Impact amplification: increase sampling multiplier when signals fire (latency spikes, error rate > 2%, sudden cost delta, model quality regression on evaluators).
Burst capture: if impact_score > 0.8, capture 100% of requests for the affected user_id or route for 5 minutes, recorded as a 'burst' event in ledger.
Downsampling rules: cap per-customer captures to 1k/day to prevent noisy customers from consuming budget.
Privacy: never log full prompt text by default; store only prompt fingerprint and small context window (first 128 bytes) if absolutely required and flagged.
console_integration: New 'Routing Verdicts' Console tab with filters: time window, region, tier, model_variant, decision_reason, request_id.
Pre-built panels: fallback rate heatmap, per-variant latency histogram, per-region cost delta trend, recent burst captures.
Alerting rules: fallback_rate > 3x baseline for 10 minutes -> slack + oncall page alert; excess storage -> infra alert.
RCA workflow: from a sampled verdict link open full archived payload (ACL-guarded) and create an incident with pre-populated fields.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for sampler math and token-bucket enforcement.
Integration tests: end-to-end emit -> kafka -> ClickHouse pipeline with synthetic high-impact scenarios.
Canary plan: enable sampling in eu-west1 for 24h at 10x baseline to validate volume and Console UX before global rollout.
E2E QA: simulate model variant rollout that triggers quality regressions and verify a captured burst event appears in Console and archived payloads.
work_items: W1: Spike (2d) to implement prototype sampler in sidecar and measure emitted bandwidth in staging.
W2: Schema PR for verdict ledger; proto + migration scripts.
W3: ClickHouse table and ingestion pipeline; retention and downsample jobs.
W4: Console UI: filters and panels; link to archived payload viewer.
W5: Alerting rules and runbook update; SRE review.
W6: Security review and ACL config for archived payloads.
W7: Canary rollout and monitor for 72h, collect feedback and iterate.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sampling surge could exceed storage budget -> Mitigation: global token-bucket gating and emergency kill-switch feature flag.
Risk: Logged artifacts may inadvertently include sensitive prompt fragments -> Mitigation: strict redaction rules and privacy gating; security review required for any schema change.
Risk: High-cardinality filters lead to slow Console queries -> Mitigation: pre-aggregations in ClickHouse and query timeouts.
